title: What's happening?
ringsNote: Each moment has its own circles. Change them with "rings": ripple, outward, tide, loosen, warm, open, still or fade.
intro: Pick what's closest. Each one has three short steps: notice it, interrupt it, then finish with something real.
doneLine: That's done. You can file this one away.

signs: Running back over what you said, or what they said, again and again
Rehearsing what you should have said instead
Scanning for signs you got it wrong, or that they're annoyed
recognise.naming: This is a replay. My brain is trying to keep me safe by going over it.

drills.name: Kind pause
lines: If a friend told me they'd said this, what would I say to them?
Can I say that to myself, even a little?

drills.name: Notice the thought
drills.prompt: Type the line that keeps coming back.

then.question: Is there one small thing I want to do about this?
then.hint: Like sending a short message, or asking a question later.
then.yes: Then pick a time for it, and let it rest until then.
then.no: Then it can be done. It happened, it's over, and it doesn't need more of you.

actions: Make a cup of tea and drink it sitting down
Wash, dry and put away one cup
Walk to the end of the road and back

signs: Thoughts starting with "what if…"
Jumping to the worst way things could go
Feeling you have to keep thinking about it, or something bad will happen
recognise.naming: This is worrying about the future. It feels urgent, but it isn't happening right now.

drills.name: Worry tree
drills.first: What exactly am I worried about?
drills.firstHint: A few words, or skip. Nothing you type is kept.
drills.can: Is there anything I can do about it?
drills.cantSay: Then it's a 'what if' worry. You can let it go for now, or park it for later.
drills.nowSay: Then do that one thing. That's your completing step.

complete.intro: If you did the one thing, that's it. Otherwise:
actions: Write tomorrow's first small task on a sticky note and put it where you'll see it
Tidy one surface: clear it, wipe it, done
Make a snack and eat it

signs: "Why did I…?", "Why am I like this?", "Why does this always happen?"
Going round in circles without getting anywhere new
Feeling worse the longer you think, not clearer
recognise.naming: This is a 'why' loop. 'Why' questions rarely have an ending, so my brain keeps going round and round.

drills.name: How, not why
drills.intro: Three questions, one at a time. Type, or just think.
lines: How, step by step, did it actually happen? Just the facts, like a camera would see it.
At which step could something have gone a little differently?
What's one small thing I'd try next time at that step?
drills.outro: That's the useful part of the thinking done. The rest can stop.

actions: Write your 'next time' line on paper and put it somewhere you'll see it
Make your bed, or straighten one room
Take a shower or wash your face, start to finish

moments.title: The same thought on repeat

signs: One sentence, image or tune going round and round
The harder you try not to think it, the louder it gets
It feels sticky, like your attention is stuck to it
recognise.naming: This is a sticky thought. I don't have to argue with it or get rid of it.

actions: Put on one song you like and listen to the whole thing
Do one small hands-on task: fold a basket of washing, water the plants
Step outside, notice three things, come back in

moments.helpNote: If the thought is about harm, contamination or checking, have a look at Get help now.

signs: Tired body, busy mind
Lists, plans or the day's moments replaying in bed
Checking the time and worrying about not sleeping
recognise.naming: This is a busy mind at bedtime. It's trying to finish the day's business.

drills.name: Brain dump
drills.prompt: Type everything that's in your head, in any order. Half-sentences are fine.

actions: Put the phone face down, out of reach
Get a glass of water, drink half, set it by the bed
Turn the light off yourself, as a deliberate "day over" moment

signs: Calling yourself names, or "you always…" / "you never…"
A tone you'd never use with someone else
Feeling smaller, or wanting to hide
recognise.naming: This is my inner critic. I hear it because it speaks loudly, not because it speaks the truth.

drills.name: Kind pause
drills.intro: Hand on your chest or arm, if that feels okay.
lines: Lots of people feel like this. I'm not the only one.
Can I be a little kinder to myself right now?
drills.outro: What would someone who cares about me say? Think it, or type it.

actions: Do one small kind thing for your body: a glass of water, a warm drink, a jumper
Send a short hello to someone safe (no need to explain)
Write down one thing you did today, however small, and leave it at that

signs: Going quiet, numb or far away
Words, decisions or moving feel hard or impossible
Wanting to be under a blanket, in the dark, alone
recognise.naming: This may be a shutdown. My system is protecting me. Nothing needs to happen right now.

drills.name: Press and let go
lines: Press your palms together. Then let go.

actions: Take a sip of water
Change position: sit up, or lie the other way
Wrap something soft or heavy around you
complete.closing: You came back a little. That's enough for now.

moments.title: When "I have to" makes it impossible

signs: A strong "no" the moment something becomes a must, even things you want to do
Anxiety or irritation rising as the pressure builds
Doing anything except the thing
recognise.naming: This is my brain reacting to a demand. I am not lazy. My body is reacting as if there is a threat.

drills.name: Change the words
drills.prompt: What's the thing? Just a few words.
frames: I might {x}, or I might not.

drills.name: Make it smaller
lines: What's the tiniest piece of this?

drills.name: Make it yours
lines: Is there a way to do it that's more fun, different, or more your own?

drills.name: Permission
lines: You're allowed to not do it right now.
drills.outro: Sometimes that's what lets it happen.

actions: Do the tiniest piece, start to finish, then stop (stopping is allowed)
Decide "not now" and pick a time. Deciding is a finish too.

recognise.lead: You might notice, after an event, a busy day or being around lots of people:
signs: Drained, flat or irritable, even if it went well
Sounds, light or touch feel harder than usual
Replaying the event, or not wanting to talk to anyone
recognise.naming: This is a hangover from a lot of input. My battery is low. Social processing uses a lot of bandwidth.

drills.name: Not now for the replay
lines: You can look back on the event later, if you want to. Not tonight.

complete.intro: A recovery ritual with a clear end:
actions: Change into soft clothes. Taking off the day's clothes can be a "costume off" moment.
Shower or bath, start to finish
Make a simple, familiar food and eat it somewhere quiet
complete.closing: Recharging is part of the day, not just an added extra.

help.title: Get help now
help.urgentTitle: If you're in danger or thinking about ending your life

urgent.how: Text HELLO to 50808, free, any time

help.soonIntro: See your GP, or talk to a qualified therapist. It may be time if:
soon: Loops happen most days for two weeks or more, or get in the way of sleep, work or relationships

Loops are about harm, contamination or something bad happening, with urges to check, repeat or seek reassurance. A specialist approach for OCD (exposure and response prevention) helps more than these drills, and some drills here can accidentally feed it.
You have thoughts about not wanting to be here, even if they come and go
help.ongoing: Ebbly is made by Brian Boland, psychotherapist (IACP), in Marino, Dublin 3 and online.
help.directoryNote: You can also find a therapist near you through the IACP.
help.privacy: This is a self-help tool, not therapy or medical care. Nothing you type leaves your phone, and nothing typed is kept.
